name: Swiss chard
tile_uses: The soup, the orecchiette, the farro bowls, the minestrone
why_now: Chard is one of the greens that does best in Southern California's cool season. It's tender enough to cook in minutes and sturdy enough for a pot of soup.
how_to_choose: Glossy, upright leaves with no yellowing
Crisp stems that snap rather than bend
Any color — rainbow, red, or white — cooks the same
buy_this_much: 3 bunches for the suggested week: the soup, the orecchiette, and the farro bowls (and a frittata).

flavor_paths.name: In soup
flavor_paths.description: Stems early, leaves at the end.

flavor_paths.name: With pasta
flavor_paths.description: With melted leeks, chile, and Parmesan.

weekday_uses: Stirred into the beef and white bean soup
Wilted through orecchiette with sausage and leeks
Wilted into the braise juices for the farro bowls
Stems early and leaves late in the minestrone
weekend_use: Stems and leaves folded into a chard and Parmesan frittata.
storage: In the fridge, wrapped loosely in a damp towel in a bag, for up to five days.
one_thing_to_learn: Chard is two vegetables. The stems need five minutes longer than the leaves, so chop them and start them first; add the leaves at the end, when they only need to wilt.
